result.topic_en: Computing the Briggsian (base-10) logarithm modulus M = log e ≈ 0.4342944819 to many decimal places, using a close rational approximation whose numerator and denominator factor into primes below 1100 (the limit of Sharp's table), and adding the resulting partial-fraction decimal expansions.

methods.what: Approximating the modulus of Briggsian logarithms by a fraction whose numerator and denominator factor into primes smaller than 1100, so that factor tables can be used
methods.quote: benutzt man einen sehr nahe kommenden Bruch, dessen Zähler und Nenner sich in Factoren zerlegen lassen, alle kleiner als 1100 (die Grenze der Sharpschen Tafel.

methods.what: Rational approximation to the modulus and its prime factorization
Prime factorization of the approximating fraction
Partial-fraction decomposition of f over the prime factors of the denominator
Summation of the long decimal expansions of the partial fractions to obtain the modulus to about 35 decimals, compared with the true value
